quickAnswer: **Google Analytics 4** is the default choice when you need **free, deep web and app analytics** with Google Ads and Search Console integration — especially at scale. Skip it if you want privacy-first simplicity, self-hosting, or to avoid cookie consent complexity — **Plausible**, **Fathom**, or **Matomo** are cleaner fits.
bestFor: Marketing teams running **Google Ads** or relying on Google marketing ecosystem
Sites and apps that need **event-based measurement** at high volume without per-hit SaaS fees
Organizations comfortable with **BigQuery export** for custom analysis
Teams that already have GA4 expertise and reporting workflows
notFor: Small sites that only need simple traffic stats and want minimal compliance overhead
Teams avoiding Google data processing or US cloud jurisdiction concerns
Privacy-first positioning without cookie banners — lightweight tools win here
Revenue attribution for indie Stripe SaaS without significant GA4 ecommerce setup — **DataFast** is simpler

sections.title: Measurement model
sections.content:
GA4 uses an **event-based data model** — every interaction is an event with parameters. Pageviews, scrolls, purchases, and custom actions all flow through the same pipeline. This replaces Universal Analytics' session/pageview-centric model and requires relearning reports and explorations.

Strength: flexible schema for web + app in one property. Weakness: easy to over-instrument and inflate event counts, making reports noisy without governance.

For marketing sites, start with **enhanced measurement** defaults and add custom events only where decisions depend on them.

sections.title: Google ecosystem & integrations
sections.content:
GA4's biggest advantage is **integration depth**: Google Ads linking, Search Console, Looker Studio, and optional **BigQuery export** (standard properties get limited free export; 360 unlocks more). If your growth stack is Google-centric, GA4 is the hub.

Non-Google integrations exist via GTM and APIs but are rarely as seamless as native Google links. Teams on Meta Ads or other channels often still run GA4 alongside platform pixels.

Consent Mode v2 and regional settings matter for EU traffic — misconfiguration can skew attribution and create compliance risk.

sections.title: How much does Google Analytics cost?
sections.content:
**Standard Google Analytics 4 is free.** Google Analytics 360 is the paid enterprise tier, sold as an annual contract through Google or a Google Sales Partner; Google doesn't publish a list price.

What 360 buys you is higher limits and SLAs:

| Limit | GA4 (free) | GA4 360 |
|---|---|---|
| Event data retention (explorations) | 2 or 14 months | Up to 50 months |
| Event-scoped custom dimensions | 50 per property | 125 per property |
| Key events | 30 | 50 |
| Audiences | 100 | 400 |
| Explore sampling limit | 10M events per query | 1B events per query |
| BigQuery daily export | 1M events | Billions of events |
| Data API quota | 200,000 tokens/day | 2M tokens/day |
| Service level agreement | No | Yes |

**Hidden costs of "free" GA4:** consent-banner and legal work in GDPR regions, Tag Manager setup and maintenance, and BigQuery storage and query charges billed by Google Cloud if you use the export. Large properties on the free tier are limited to 2 months of event-data retention.

Most sites never need 360. If you are paying for GA4 mainly to avoid consent banners or data-transfer concerns, compare cookie-free tools like [Plausible](/tools/plausible/), [Fathom](/tools/fathom/) or [Ahrefs Web Analytics](/tools/ahrefs/), or use our [pricing calculator](/calculators/pricing/).

sections.title: Privacy & compliance
sections.content:
GA4 is **not** a privacy-first tool in the Plausible sense. It uses cookies and identifiers, processes data on Google infrastructure, and typically requires **consent banners** in GDPR jurisdictions.

Google offers **data retention controls**, IP anonymization options (context-dependent), and user deletion tools — but operational burden falls on you. Several EU regulators have scrutinized Google Analytics transfers; some organizations choose Matomo or EU-hosted alternatives for that reason.

Free does not mean zero compliance cost — legal review and consent UX are part of the total price.

If consent banners or data transfers are the main reason you are looking at alternatives, compare a [free cookie-free alternative such as Ahrefs Web Analytics](/tools/ahrefs/).

setupNotes:
**Typical setup:**

1. Create a GA4 property and web data stream.
2. Install **gtag.js** or deploy via **Google Tag Manager**.
3. Configure **key events** (conversions) and link Google Ads if applicable.
4. Set data retention, internal traffic filters, and consent defaults.
5. Validate with DebugView before trusting reports.

**Common pitfalls:** duplicate tags inflating counts, missing consent mode in EU, treating GA4 like UA reports, and unbounded custom events without naming conventions.
pricingNotes:
GA4 standard is **free** for most sites within Google's collection limits. **Google Analytics 360** is a custom-priced annual contract (contact Google or a Sales Partner) for very large organizations needing SLAs, higher limits, and advanced BigQuery.

Hidden costs: GTM/consulting time, BigQuery storage/query bills, and compliance tooling. At low traffic, GA4 wins on price vs any paid privacy tool; at high traffic, "free" still holds for standard tier but ops complexity grows.

Use our [pricing calculator](/calculators/pricing/) to compare GA4 ($0) against paid alternatives at your pageview level.
limitations: Steep learning curve vs Plausible/Fathom — reports are powerful but not simple.
Privacy and EU transfer concerns push some teams to Matomo or EU-hosted tools.
No session replay or heatmaps natively — pair with Hotjar or PostHog.
Revenue attribution for custom Stripe flows requires deliberate ecommerce/event setup.
Script weight and performance vary by implementation — benchmark pending on AnalyticsVS.

faq.question: Is GA4 still free?
faq.answer: Yes, the standard GA4 property is free for typical site and app volumes. Enterprise 360 is a separate paid product.

faq.question: GA4 vs Universal Analytics — what changed?
faq.answer: GA4 is event-based, uses different reports, and UA stopped processing in 2023. You cannot expect one-to-one metric parity with old UA dashboards.

faq.question: Do I need Google Tag Manager?
faq.answer: Not required, but GTM is the standard way to manage tags without code deploys. Simple sites can use gtag.js directly.

faq.question: When should I pick Plausible instead?
faq.answer: When you want simple traffic analytics, fewer compliance headaches, and do not depend on Google Ads native reporting.

faq.question: How much does Google Analytics 360 cost?
faq.answer: Google Analytics 360 is sold as a custom annual contract through Google or a Sales Partner, and Google does not publish a list price. It mainly buys higher limits (for example up to 50 months of event data retention vs 14, and billions of daily BigQuery export events vs 1 million) plus SLAs.

faq.question: What are the limits of free GA4?
faq.answer: Free GA4 keeps event-level data for explorations for 2 or 14 months, allows 30 key events and 50 event-scoped custom dimensions, and exports 1 million events per day to BigQuery. Standard aggregated reports are not affected by the retention setting.
